bib.title: VERA: Scaling Verifiable Environments for Agentic co-Evolution

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "VERA: Scaling Verifiable Environments for Agentic co-Evolution". First author Junqi Liu (UCSC); senior and project lead Yucheng Tang (NVIDIA). Other authors from NVIDIA, UIUC, NUS, Tsinghua, Xian Jiaotong and UPenn. arXiv:2610.05923v1 [cs.AI], dated 5 Oct 2026 (header "2026-10-6"). Preprint, no venue. The repo file is liu-2026-vera.pdf.

COVERAGE: 27 of 27 pages read, 87,888 chars, including appendices A–I. References were skimmed.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. [Note 05 post-training for agents; note 06 data and environments] Co-evolving the model and the harness beats either axis alone. At 9B, the full loop beats the best single-axis baseline by 10.3 points (CoWork) and 13.0 points (Med).
 - Setup: Qwen3.5-9B. AutoCoWorkBench and AutoMedBench-Lite Overall, which averages Agentic and Task. The AutoCoWorkBench release protocol averages 3 seeds (App. A.1). The paper does not say how many seeds produced the Table 2 numbers. No variance is reported.
 - Numbers (Table 2): CoWork full 31.0, VERA Harness only 18.2, VERA LLM only 18.9, ADAS 20.7. Med full 69.1, harness only 56.1, LLM only 43.3, ADAS 55.5.
 - Quote: "On AutoCoWorkBench, VERA-Code Agent reaches 31.0 Overall, exceeding the strongest single-axis baseline, ADAS (20.7), by 10.3 points." (p.7)
 - Quote: "Freezing one axis costs about half the gain... LLM-only reaches 43.3 and harness-only 56.1, against 69.1 for the full loop; on AutoCoWorkBench, 18.9 and 18.2 against 31.0." (p.7)
 - Base is 4.2 (CoWork) and 19.9 (Med). Official-scorer Pass@1 for the full method: SWE-Bench Verified 54.2, MedXpertQA Text 50.8.
2. [Notes 07 reward design, 08 reasoning RL] Rubric-based stage rewards beat outcome-only GRPO, which collapses in this setting. Baselines were matched at 500 updates, which is five 100-update VERA rounds (Table 13).
 - 9B CoWork Overall: GRPO 5.8 (SWE-Bench P@1 14.8, below the base's 41.8), SFT 6.7, RaR 18.1, OPD 19.8, ReflectRL 17.3, COS-PLAY 19.9.
 - 9B Med Overall: GRPO 36.3, RaR 31.9, OPD 41.2, ReflectRL 28.6, COS-PLAY 26.4, SFT 12.9.
 - GRPO here uses "an outcome-only reward derived from verified rubrics" (App. F.1). RaR adds item-level process credit.
 - VERA LLM-only (GRPO with rubric stage rewards and verifier) gets 18.9 CoWork and 43.3 Med. It is not clearly better than OPD or RaR on CoWork.
3. [Note 10 engineering RL systems; note 05] Scaling to 27B (Qwen3.8-27B) reaches near-frontier scores, using benchmark-default runners (Table 3).
 - Scores: VERA-CoWork-27B Agent 71.6 vs GPT-5.6-Sol 72.6, Claude-Opus-4.8 66.6, base 63.8. VERA-Med-27B Agent 80.7 vs Opus-4.8 81.9, GPT-5.6-Sol 75.1, base 65.1.
 - Quote: "VERA scores 71.6 on AutoCoWorkBench, 1.0 point below GPT-5.6-Sol, and 80.7 on AutoMedBench, 1.2 points below Claude-Opus-4.8." (p.8)
 - The abstract and intro claim it "surpasses" the baseline or Opus 4.8 on AutoCoWorkBench. That holds only against Opus and not against GPT-5.6-Sol. Under the productivity harnesses in Fig. 2, VERA is highest on both. Rankings flip with the harness: Claude scores 80.5 with its productivity harness and 81.9 with the benchmark default.
 - Transfer, not used in training: Automation-Bench 43.8% (+19.2 pp, rank 2). AgentClinic 76.4% (+32.5 pp, rank 3).
 - At 27B, only VERA LLM-only and harness-only variants are compared, with no matched baselines.
4. [Notes 06, 07] Environment construction (Auto-Rubric).
 - It uses 9,000+ open environments built from benchmark trajectories (Terminal-Bench, SWE-Bench, MLE-Bench, AutoMedBench, MedXpertQA).
 - Each workflow is split into 5 restartable stages: plan, setup, verify, execute, submit.
 - Rubrics are binary. Executable checks override judge scores. An Agent Judge inspects the workspace.
 - Reward: r_k = h_k · Σw·z / Σw. End-to-end reward R_e2e = g[λp + (1−λ)c], with λ=0.2 for CoWork and λ=0.5 for Med. A verified hack sets g=0 (the hard gate).
 - GRPO advantage: A_i = (R_i − mean R)/(std R + 1e-6).
 - Acceptance gates: a model checkpoint is accepted if its dev score drops no more than 20% relative to the last accepted one. A harness edit needs a paired rerun, an Overall gain of at least 5 pp, no end-to-end regression and a pass on safety checks. At most 3 edits are accepted per round.
5. [Notes 05, 10] General-capability retention depends on scale (Table 4).
 - 4B and 9B degrade sharply. AIME 2026: Qwen3.5-9B 92.5 falls to 36.7 (CoWork) and 76.7 (Med). 4B falls 56.4 to 59.7 points.
 - 27B CoWork improves on all four benchmarks (AIME 86.7→96.7, GPQA 82.2→89.9). 27B Med: AIME +3.3, GPQA +5.6, ALFWorld −4.0, IF-Bench −0.7.
 - Quote: "The 4B and 9B agents decline on several benchmarks, with AIME losses of 56.4-59.7 and 15.8-55.8 points, respectively." (p.8)
6. [Note 10] Cost.
 - Medical pipeline replacement-cost estimate is about $240k. Environment scaling and curation take 54.7%, training infrastructure 27.9%, and verification, judging and attribution 17.3%.
 - 27B run: about 5,000 H100-hours (CoWork) and 8,000 H100-hours (Med).
 - Training settings: 12×8 rollouts (CoWork) and 8×8 (Med), Adam, BF16, full-parameter GRPO. The seed is given only for the SFT init (260910).
 - The curves are "illustrative", not measured spend (p.8).

LIMITS (authors, Sec. 6, p.10, plus appendix caveats)
- Environment count and construction method are not varied.
- Harness and reasoning-effort settings are not ablated.
- Judge, verifier and attribution all use GPT-5.6-Sol, and judge sensitivity is untested.
- Full baseline comparisons exist only at 9B.
- Rubrics-as-Rewards is held fixed, so reward formulation and update operators are not ablated.
- Not stated by the authors, but visible in the tables:
  - No seeds or confidence intervals for Table 2.
  - Gains at 9B vs 27B are confounded: Qwen3.5 supplies 4B and 9B, and Qwen3.8 supplies 27B.
  - The ADAS search was degenerate: all 27 eligible candidates scored zero on the selection metric, so the first was picked (App. F.3). The paper says this "does not establish a development performance gain".
  - The COS-PLAY baseline is a reduced adaptation: 200 updates, SFT-200 init, no original LoRA setup.
  - Harness case study: 1 of 6 tasks vs 0 of 6, with logs unavailable. Verifier audit: 64 rollouts, record consistency only, not judgement correctness.
  - The AutoCoWorkBench Lite core is only 40 tasks. The Med harness lift and the 27B Med base-plus-VERA-Harness result are worse than base (54.2 vs 65.1).
  - The authors own the benchmarks (AutoMedBench, from Liu et al. 2026b, and the 9,000-environment sources).

BUILDS ON: GRPO (Shao et al., 2024), RaR (Gunjal et al., 2025), OPD (Agarwal et al., 2024), ReflectRL (Bi et al., 2026), ADAS (Hu et al., 2025), COS-PLAY (Wu et al., 2026b), Agent Lightning (Luo et al., 2025), Benchmark-as-Teacher (Liu et al., 2026a), Agent-as-a-judge (Zhuge et al., 2024), DeepSeek-R1 (2025). A note on the dating: the references include future-dated arXiv ids, such as 2610.05923.

CODE: none beyond the equations above (p.5 and App. E.2).

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p.2) is the co-evolution loop, with attribution, verifiers and fallback. Fig. 3 (p.4) is Auto-Rubric, the five stages and the admission checks. Fig. 2 (p.3) shows the scale and frontier comparison. Fig. 5 (p.25) is a worked report-driven example.

PROBLEMS: Extraction was clean. There were no embedded instructions. Fractional table symbols and the tables in the appendix extracted fine. The bold markers for best scores were lost in Table 2.
